subject: Biotechnology
title: The Promise and Limits of Personalized Medicine
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Promise and Limits of Personalized Medicine usable.

hook.text: Personalized medicine promises the right treatment for each patient — but most prescriptions are still one-size-fits-all.

buildup.text: Genomic data generation far outpaces clinical implementation — hospitals lack infrastructure to use results routinely.

discovery.text: Health disparities widen when genomics serves only wealthy populations — equitable access is an ethical imperative.

twist.text: Common diseases are influenced by environment as much as genetics — genes are just one piece of the puzzle.

climax.text: The vision: every patient's genome in their health record, guiding every medical decision for their entire life.

punchline.text: Personalized medicine is a promise in progress — genomics leads, healthcare follows.

quiz.question: What is the main barrier to widespread personalized medicine adoption?
options: Genomic sequencing is still too expensive for any hospital
Clinical infrastructure and equitable access lag behind the pace of genomic data generation
Patients do not want their genomes sequenced
